2. This Criminal Miscellaneous Application
has been filed by the applicant seeking
quashing of the orders dated 17.07.2026 and
22.09.2026 passed by the learned Sessions
Judge, Haridwar, in Criminal Appeal No.116
of 2026.
3. Facts of the case, in brief, are that the
applicant was convicted for the offence
punishable under Section 138 of the
Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 vide
judgment and order dated 28.07.2025 passed
by learned Additional Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar, in Criminal Case
No.3356 of 2024. The applicant was
sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment
for a period of six months and was further
directed to pay a fine of ₹9,50,000/-. Out of
the aforesaid amount, ₹9,30,000/- was
directed to be paid to respondent no.2
towards compensation, while the remaining
amount of ₹20,000/- was directed to be
deposited in the State Treasury. In default of
payment of fine, the applicant was directed to
undergo additional simple imprisonment for a
period of one month.

4. Aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment
and order of conviction, the applicant
preferred Criminal Appeal No.116 of 2026
before the learned Sessions Judge, Haridwar,
along with an application seeking suspension
of sentence and grant of bail. Learned
Sessions Judge, vide order dated 15.06.2026
granted bail to the applicant. Thereafter, on
17.07.2026, learned Sessions Judge directed
the applicant to deposit 20% of the fine
amount before the learned trial Court within
a period of 30 days. Thereafter, the applicant
moved an application seeking modification of
the aforesaid condition on the ground that he
was unable to arrange the requisite amount
and prayed that the amount of deposit be
reduced to 10% and that one month's further
time be granted for depositing the same.
Learned Sessions Judge, vide order dated
24.08.2026, allowed the said application and
reduced the amount of deposit from 20% to
10%. It is the case of the applicant that,
owing to his financial inability, he could not
deposit even the reduced amount within the
stipulated period. Consequently, he moved
another application seeking extension of one
month's time to deposit the amount. However,
learned Sessions Judge, vide order dated
22.09.2026, rejected the said application and
cancelled the bail granted to the applicant.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant
submits that Section 148 of the N.I. Act
empowers the Appellate Court to direct an
appellant, who has been convicted for an
offence under Section 138 of the N.I. Act, to
deposit an amount which shall not be less
than 20% of the fine or compensation
awarded by the learned trial Court. He
submits that, once the Appellate Court
decides to impose a condition of deposit
under the aforesaid provision, it cannot
reduce the amount below the statutory
minimum of 20%.
6. Learned counsel further submits that
the applicant had not deliberately disobeyed
the condition imposed by the Appellate Court

but was unable to comply with the same on
account of financial constraints. He submits
that the learned Appellate Court, without
properly considering the circumstances
pleaded by the applicant, rejected his prayer
for extension of time and cancelled the bail
already granted to him. Learned counsel for
the applicant submits that Hon'ble Supreme
Court in Muskan Enterprises and Another v.
The State of Punjab and Another, reported in
(2024) 20 SCC 85, has considered the scope
of the Appellate Court's power under Section
148 of the N.I. Act and observed that, once
the Appellate Court considers a deposit
necessary, it may, in an appropriate case,
direct the appellant to deposit an amount
exceeding 20% of the fine or compensation
awarded by the trial Court, therefore, the
impugned order deserves to be set aside.
7. In view of the aforesaid legal position,
the impugned orders dated 17.07.2026 and
22.09.2026, passed by learned Sessions
Judge, Haridwar, cannot be sustained and
are liable to be set aside.
8. Accordingly, the impugned orders dated
17.07.2026 and 22.09.2026 passed by the
learned Sessions Judge, Haridwar, in
Criminal Appeal No.116 of 2026, are hereby
set aside.
9. The criminal misc. application is,
accordingly, disposed of.
 (Alok Mahra, J.) 31.10.2026
Arpan
